canonical_topic: Continuous injection/withdrawal requirement for pipeline operation
definition: A pipeline only functions because gas is continuously injected at the high-pressure (supply) end and continuously withdrawn at the low-pressure (consumer) end; if either side stops for economic reasons, the pressure differential collapses and the pipeline stops moving gas.
core_idea: Because pipeline flow depends entirely on maintaining a pressure gradient, operators may have to keep injecting and withdrawing gas even when it looks uneconomical, since restarting a stalled pipeline takes significant time.
key_points: Gas only flows from high-pressure zones to low-pressure zones
Injections and withdrawals cannot be halted purely because they are unprofitable at a given moment without risking pipeline shutdown
Restarting a pipeline after a stoppage takes time, so it may need to keep running even with no active consumer demand and no available storage
relationships: Compressor stations maintain this pressure differential
Explains why pipeline operators rely on interruptible customers to keep pressure up
trading_implications: Pipeline operators have structural reasons to keep moving gas regardless of short-term economics, which affects how reliably interruptible capacity is offered
caveats: Assuming pipeline flow can be freely started and stopped like a valve, without consequence for the broader network
